people we knew in this life and also those who may have no one to pray for them. many people choose to commemorate their deceased family and friends by adding their names to the parish altar list of the dead. it’s an important tradition to maintain every year as those whose names are on the altar list of the dead are remembered regularly at masses throughout the year. our gospel today is the beatitudes which can be described as a charter for christian living which perfectly describe her life. reading it today, it appears to be counter cultural as it turns many of today’s values on their head. they go to the very centre of our lives as christians and invite us to follow a way of life that may not come naturally to us. however, the very words that jesus uses here “gentle”, “merciful”, “pure in heart”, “peacemaker” are an appropriate description of kay’s g ood and generous life. jesus also challenges us by referring to those who hunger and thirst for what is right”. pope benedict tried to explain the meaning of life after death within the limitations of our language and understanding. i hope that their reflections below will offer some consolation especially to those amongst us who may have lost a friend or family member in the past year and are particularly feeling their absence around now. when speaking about the next life in 2012, pope benedict xvi sa id: “death opens to life, to eternal life, which is not an infinite duplicate of the present time, but something completely new.” in a beautiful reflection, pope benedict goes on to explain that: “our hope, then, lies in the love of god that shines resp lendent from the cross of christ who lets jesus’ words to the good thief: “today you will be with me in paradise” (lk 23:43) resound in our heart.” saint john henry newman in his poem “the dream of gerontius” describes the soul, approaching heaven, as it sees something of the divine vision: “a grand mysterious harmony: it floods me, like the deep and solemn sound of many waters.” pope john xxiii, now a saint, was once asked if he prayed for the dead. he replied: “i often think of the departed, they keep me good company.” there is an unbroken chain of connection with our beloved dead, who continue to pray for us in the presence of god, and ourselves as we continue to pray for them. we can be especially close to them during when we celebrate mass when our deceased relatives and friends are always remembered in the eucharistic prayer. may they rest in peace. amen. let us continue to pray for and remember our faithful departed during the month from: navan road community council we attended a public meeting of residents' concerns, re; fingal co. council's'dunsink urban area draft plan' to develop former green belt lands at scribblestown/ dunsink dump - directly below dunsink observatory, for approx. 16,000 housing units.

concerns raised were:- loss of green belt & trees; over density; lack of schools and public transport; the plan refers to'buses along n3/ navan road' & 'ashtown & navan road train stations as public transport hubs'. we all know how full our public transport is at peak times.
